To introduce integral feedback into an LQR setting, we augment the system by adding a new state variable q(t) that represents the integral of the system state that we want to go to zero. The poles of the closed-loop dynamics are the eigenvalues of the matrix A - BK. To find the eigenvalues of a matrix M, we can solve the characteristic equation |M - λI| = 0.

For the closed-loop dynamics, the characteristic equation is:

|A - BK - λI| = 0

Expanding the determinant, we get:

|A - λI - BK| = 0

Since P↵ is the stabilizing solution to the Riccati equation, the matrix P↵ is positive definite and thus the matrix BK = -BT P↵ is negative definite. Therefore, all the eigenvalues of the matrix A - BK have a negative real part.

Furthermore, since we have e↵t as a weighting factor in our performance function, Re(λ) < -↵, which means the closed-loop poles all lie in the half plane {z 2 C : Re(z) < -↵}. This means that the closed-loop system is stable, and the state variables will converge to zero asymptotically.
